stem.text: Let \( y = f(x) \) be the particular solution to the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x}{y} \) with \( f(5) = 3 \). The largest open interval containing \( x = 5 \) on which the solution exists has exactly one finite endpoint. Find that endpoint.

worked_solution.text: Separate and antidifferentiate: \( \frac{y^{2}}{2} = \frac{x^{2}}{2} + C \), so \( y^{2} = x^{2} + 2C \).
At \( (5, 3) \): \( 2C = -16 \), and the positive root applies, so \( y = \sqrt{x^{2} - 16} \).
The expression needs \( x^{2} > 16 \), because at \( x^{2} = 16 \) \( y = 0 \) and \( \frac{dy}{dx} \) is undefined.
The piece containing \( x = 5 \) is \( \left(4, \infty\right) \), so the finite endpoint is \( 4 \).
